All 16 views complete. Summary of analysis:

**Test image**: Corn ear with white/gray cottony mold growing over kernels in the middle section, with some brownish discolored kernels beneath. Yellow healthy kernels visible on both sides.

**Comparison results**:
- **Fusarium_Disease**: Best match — reference (Corn_Disease_25.jpg) shows white cottony mold scattered across kernels in the middle of the ear, matching the test image closely in color, texture, and distribution pattern
- **Diplodia_Ear_Rot**: Grayish-brown mummified appearance, not fluffy white mold — less similar
- **Aspergillus_Ear_Rot**: Olive-green powdery mold — clearly different color
- **Common_Smut**: Large distinctive black galls — clearly different
- **Gibberella_Disease**: Pink/purple on husks — different color entirely
- **Trichoderma_Ear_Rot**: Dark blue-green conidia — different color
- **Head_Smut**: Dark brown spore masses — different
- All leaf diseases: Not applicable (ear affected)

The white/gray cottony growth scattered on yellow kernels in the test image is the hallmark visual of Fusarium_Disease, matching the reference images closely.
